text: Write a program that builds a string in a loop with a running trace, so an off-by-one in the separator becomes visible. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: System.out.println("[" + sb + "]");   // [a, b, c] with no trailing comma
explanation: Verified: `[a, b, c]`. Drop the condition and you get `[a, b, c, ]` — the trailing-separator bug, which is small, universal, and a good illustration of why the loop's boundaries deserve as much attention as its body. `String.join(", ", xs)` does this correctly and is what you should actually write; building it once by hand is how you learn to see the boundary.
